interpretation.diagram_classification: cosmological (probable diagram of the four elements and their qualities, or of the four cardinal points / four seasons; schematic, unlabelled)
interpretation.interpretation: The diagram most probably shows a cosmological scheme in which a square frame (the world or the cosmos) encloses a diamond formed by four circles joined by bands. The four corner circles, each in a different colour (dark red with grid, pale grey-green, black-grey, green), may stand for the four elements (fire, air, earth, water) or the four seasons or humours, and the four rimmed circles at the midpoints of the frame sides may stand for the four cardinal points or the four qualities (hot, cold, wet, dry), which link the elements in pairs through the diamond. The vertical and horizontal lines inside the diamond form an incomplete cross or axis, possibly a measuring or orientation device. This reading is tentative: the diagram has no transcribed text, and the identification of the elements and of the corner colours is conjectural.
interpretation.evidence: There is no text in the diagram, so the interpretation rests only on visible features: a square frame with marked corners, four rimmed circles at the midpoints of its sides joined in a diamond by orange bands, and four coloured circles in the corners, each a different colour. The pattern of four coloured units and four linking points recalls medieval diagrams of the four elements and their qualities, but the colours do not match one fixed scheme, so no specific source is named. Step 1 problems: entries 2, 7, 8 and 14 relate the midpoint circles to the green frame with 'connected_to', although the circles only overlap the frame and are not joined by a line. The first entry's element name 'upper left red grid circle' is acceptable, but no relation was recorded for the four corner circles and the diamond bands as a whole, and the small corner marks at the frame corners were not recorded as elements. The vertical and horizontal lines are described as a T-junction, but the horizontal line does not clearly connect to the two lower bands.
